title: Edmund and the Vow
premise: Oscar Blackwood, a ghostwriter who has spent a decade lending pieces of his heart to other people's stories, is hired to write the memoirs of celebrated novelist Vivian Ashford — and discovers in her archive an unsent letter he wrote eleven years ago to a woman named Edmund's mother, returned unopened. The letter pulls him back to the coastal town of Porthollow, where festival season reunites him with Edmund Hale, now the town's solicitor and the son of the woman Oscar once loved and abandoned out of duty. As Oscar ghosts Vivian's memoir by day and unravels why his letter was never delivered by night, he learns Edmund has spent his life keeping a vow to protect his mother's silence — a silence that conceals a contested inheritance and the truth of who really wronged whom. When the festival ends, Oscar must choose between finishing the memoir that will make his career and exposing the truth that could break both families open; he risks the whole heart at last, confessing everything publicly, and wins not absolution but a beginning with Edmund.
about_author: Emrys Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's unsent letters before turning to fiction. They live on the Cornish coast, where every tide seems to return something someone once gave up on.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In London, Oscar signs a lucrative contract to ghostwrite Vivian Ashford's memoirs, rehearsing his creed that the heart is trainable and containable. Sorting her archive, he finds his own eleven-year-old letter, postmarked Porthollow, returned unopened. Emotional beat: controlled detachment cracking into vertigo as the past acquires a return address.

chapters.title: Postmark, Eleven Years
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He travels to Porthollow during festival preparations, telling himself it's research. At the harbor bookshop he collides with Edmund Hale — the boy from that summer, now the town solicitor, guarded and precise. Neither names the letter. Emotional beat: recognition disguised as politeness, old grief wearing new clothes.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Silence
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund recognizes Oscar instantly and resents how completely. Bound by a deathbed vow to his mother, Maren, never to speak of that summer or the inheritance dispute with the Blackwood estate, he watches Oscar interview townsfolk for the memoir. Emotional beat: duty as armor, and the first hairline fracture in it.

chapters.title: What Vivian Kept
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Memoir sessions reveal Vivian knew Maren intimately — they were rivals for the same house, the same man, perhaps the same truth. Vivian deflects with dazzling anecdotes while withholding the year that matters. Emotional beat: Oscar realizing his employer may be both witness and architect of his heartbreak.

chapters.title: Lantern Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The festival's lantern release traps Oscar and Edmund together on the seawall; a decade of restraint gives way to one honest conversation about that summer, carefully avoiding the vow. They part almost touching. Emotional beat: warmth as threat — each man recognizing the heart refusing to stay containable.

chapters.title: The Unopened Thing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Maren's health fails; she presses Edmund harder to keep the vow, hinting the letter's return was no accident. Edmund searches her papers and finds evidence the Blackwood estate was signed away under duress — and that someone intercepted Oscar's letter deliberately. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into suspicion of the very person he vowed to protect.

chapters.title: Ghostwritten
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Vivian offers Oscar co-authorship and public credit if the memoir stays 'elegant' — meaning silent about Porthollow's inheritance. He understands: his career is being purchased with his own history. He refuses quietly and keeps digging. Emotional beat: the ghostwriter deciding to stop being a ghost in his own story.

chapters.title: Maren's Tide
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Maren, near the end, summons them both and gives Edmund permission to break the vow — but dies before explaining fully, leaving a deed fragment naming the true heir. Grief and accusation collide between Oscar and Edmund; each blames the other's family, then himself. Emotional beat: love and justice pulling in opposite directions at full strength.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, climax. At the festival's closing assembly, the contested will is read. Edmund stands, breaks his vow publicly, and produces the deed fragment proving Maren renounced her claim willingly to shield Oscar's father's debt — the letter was intercepted to keep Oscar from returning and discovering his family's shame. Emotional beat: truth as detonation; the crowd, the dead, and the two men all exposed at once.

chapters.title: Whole Heart, Lent No More
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar abandons the sanitized memoir, publishing instead a small honest book dedicated to Maren, forfeiting his career's biggest prize. On the emptied festival green, he tells Edmund he's done lending pieces. Edmund, no longer bound, chooses him freely. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — justice served outside the law, love chosen over duty, the whole heart finally risked and kept.
